answer.summary: No evidence of temporal memory mechanisms exists in Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 beyond feature-based processing; a new research direction is required to explore non-feature-based persistence under minimal input variation.
answer.content: The current body of evidence fails to identify any non-feature-based memory mechanisms, including temporal coherence, error correction, or binding under stable conditions. A focused inquiry into how such systems might maintain implicit state without explicit feature vectors is now warranted to test the plausibility of memory without representation-based encoding.
